exercises.prompt: *___ the rain, we went for a long walk.*

options.label: Despite
options.feedback: Sí. *Despite* + sustantivo (*the rain*).

options.label: Although
options.feedback: Todavía no. *Although* necesita una oración con verbo: *Although it was raining*.

options.label: Despite of
options.feedback: Todavía no. *Despite* nunca lleva *of*.

options.label: However
options.feedback: Todavía no. *However* une dos oraciones; no puede ir delante de un sustantivo.

hints: Detrás del hueco hay un sustantivo, no una oración.
¿Qué conector de contraste va con sustantivo… y sin *of*?
exercises.solution:
**Despite**: *Despite the rain, we went for a long walk.*

*Despite* (y *in spite of*) van seguidos de un sustantivo o de *-ing*. Con una oración, usarías *although*: *Although it was raining, we went for a long walk*.

exercises.prompt:
Reescribe la frase con *although*:

*It was very expensive, but we bought it.*
answers: Although it was very expensive, we bought it
Although it was very expensive we bought it
We bought it although it was very expensive
Even though it was very expensive, we bought it
Even though it was very expensive we bought it
We bought it even though it was very expensive
Though it was very expensive, we bought it
Though it was very expensive we bought it
We bought it though it was very expensive

feedback.match: Although it was very expensive, but we bought it
feedback.message: Casi: en inglés no se combinan *although* y *but*. Quita *but*.

hints: *Although* + oración, y la otra oración sin *but*.
Si empiezas con *Although*, pon coma entre las dos partes.
exercises.solution:
**Although it was very expensive, we bought it.** (o *We bought it although it was very expensive*).

*Although* ya expresa el contraste, así que *but* desaparece. Si la oración con *although* va primero, se separa con coma.

exercises.prompt:
Reescribe la frase con *despite*:

*Although she was tired, she finished the report.*
answers: Despite being tired, she finished the report
Despite being tired she finished the report
Despite her tiredness, she finished the report
Despite her tiredness she finished the report
Despite feeling tired, she finished the report
Despite feeling tired she finished the report
Despite the fact that she was tired, she finished the report
Despite the fact that she was tired she finished the report
She finished the report despite being tired
She finished the report despite the fact that she was tired
In spite of being tired, she finished the report
In spite of being tired she finished the report
In spite of her tiredness, she finished the report
In spite of her tiredness she finished the report
In spite of feeling tired, she finished the report
In spite of feeling tired she finished the report
In spite of the fact that she was tired, she finished the report
In spite of the fact that she was tired she finished the report
She finished the report in spite of being tired
She finished the report in spite of the fact that she was tired

feedback.match: Despite she was tired, she finished the report
feedback.message: Casi: *despite* no puede ir seguido de una oración. Usa *-ing* (*being tired*) o *the fact that*.

feedback.match: Despite of being tired, she finished the report

hints: *Despite* + *-ing* o sustantivo.
*She was tired* → *being tired*.
exercises.solution:
**Despite being tired, she finished the report.**

Como *despite* no admite una oración, la transformamos en *-ing* (*being tired*) o en sustantivo (*despite her tiredness*). También vale *Despite the fact that she was tired, …*, que es más largo pero correcto.

exercises.prompt: *I love the city. ___, I couldn't live there. It's far too noisy.*

options.label: However
options.feedback: Sí. *However* abre una oración nueva y marca el contraste con la anterior.

options.label: Although
options.feedback: Todavía no. *Although* introduce una oración subordinada y necesita otra principal en la misma frase.

options.label: Despite
options.feedback: Todavía no. *Despite* va seguido de un sustantivo o *-ing*, no de una coma.

options.label: Because
options.feedback: Todavía no. No hay relación de causa: hay contraste.

hints: El hueco va al principio de una oración nueva, seguido de coma.
Necesitas *sin embargo*.
exercises.solution:
**However**: *I love the city. However, I couldn't live there.*

*However* une dos oraciones independientes: va detrás de un punto (o de un punto y coma) y seguido de coma. Es el equivalente de *sin embargo*.

exercises.prompt: *My brother loves football, ___ I prefer tennis.* Marca **todas** las opciones correctas.

options.label: whereas
options.feedback: Sí. *Whereas* compara dos hechos opuestos.

options.label: while
options.feedback: Sí. *While* puede comparar dos hechos, como *whereas*.

options.label: but
options.feedback: Sí. *But* también funciona, con un registro más neutro.

options.label: despite
options.feedback: Todavía no. *Despite* necesita un sustantivo o *-ing* detrás.

hints: Comparas dos gustos opuestos.
Tres de las opciones pueden unir dos oraciones completas.
exercises.solution:
**whereas**, **while** y **but**.

*Whereas* y *while* sirven para comparar dos hechos que contrastan (*mientras que*); *but* es la opción más sencilla. *Despite* no puede ir seguido de una oración.

exercises.prompt:
Completa con un conector de causa (dos o tres palabras):

*The match was cancelled ___ the storm.*
answers: because of
due to
owing to
on account of

feedback.message: Casi: *because* solo va con una oración (*because there was a storm*). Con un sustantivo, añade una palabra.

hints: Detrás del hueco hay un sustantivo (*the storm*).
*Because* + *of*… o una expresión algo más formal con *to*.
exercises.solution:
**because of** (o *due to*, *owing to*): *The match was cancelled because of the storm.*

Con un sustantivo, se usa *because of*, o las versiones más formales *due to* y *owing to*. Con una oración, *because*: *…because there was a storm*.

answers: Even if it rains, I'll go
Even if it rains I'll go
I'll go even if it rains
Even if it rains, I will go
Even if it rains I will go
I will go even if it rains
Even if it rains, I'm going
Even if it rains I'm going
I'm going even if it rains
Even if it rains, I am going
Even if it rains I am going
I am going even if it rains

feedback.message: Casi: *aunque* con subjuntivo expresa una hipótesis (quizá llueva). En inglés eso es *even if*.

feedback.match: Even if it will rain, I'll go
feedback.message: Casi: después de *even if*, el futuro se expresa con presente, como después de *if*.

hints: *Llueva* (subjuntivo): no sabes si lloverá.
Para una hipótesis, *even if* + presente.
exercises.solution:
**Even if it rains, I'll go.**

Cuando *aunque* va con subjuntivo y plantea una hipótesis, el inglés usa *even if*. Como después de *if*, el futuro va en presente (*rains*). *Although it's raining, I'm going* sería la traducción de *aunque llueve* (un hecho).

exercises.prompt: *I'm saving money ___ I can travel around Asia next year.*

options.label: so that
options.feedback: Sí. *So that* + oración (con *can*) expresa finalidad.

options.label: in order to
options.feedback: Todavía no. *In order to* va seguido de un infinitivo, no de sujeto + verbo.

options.label: for
options.feedback: Todavía no. *For* no introduce una oración de finalidad.

options.label: because
options.feedback: Todavía no. *Because* expresa causa, no finalidad.

hints: Detrás del hueco hay sujeto + verbo (*I can travel*).
Finalidad con oración completa: *para que*.
exercises.solution:
**so that**: *I'm saving money so that I can travel around Asia next year.*

*So that* introduce una oración de finalidad, a menudo con *can, could, will* o *would*. Con infinitivo dirías *in order to travel* o simplemente *to travel*.

exercises.prompt:
Completa con un conector de finalidad negativa (tres o cuatro palabras):

*She took a taxi ___ miss the train.* (para no perder el tren)
answers: so as not to
in order not to

feedback.message: Casi: la finalidad no se expresa con *for*. Usa *so as not to* o *in order not to*.
Se oye en la conversación, pero en un texto cuidado se prefiere una forma más larga con *not* antes de *to*.

hints: *Not* va justo antes de *to*.
*So as not to* o *in order not to*.
exercises.solution:
**so as not to** (o *in order not to*): *She took a taxi so as not to miss the train.*

Para una finalidad negativa con infinitivo, *not* va antes de *to*: *so as not to*, *in order not to*. También podrías decir *so that she wouldn't miss the train*.

exercises.prompt: Escribes un ensayo formal y quieres añadir un segundo argumento al principio de un párrafo. ¿Qué conector es el más adecuado?

options.label: Furthermore,
options.feedback: Sí. Es formal y abre una oración nueva con coma.

options.label: Plus,
options.feedback: Se usa en la conversación y en textos informales, pero en un ensayo formal suena demasiado coloquial.

options.label: And also,
options.feedback: Todavía no. Empezar con *And also* es coloquial y redundante en un ensayo.

options.label: As well,
options.feedback: Todavía no. *As well* va al final de la frase, no al principio.

hints: Busca el registro formal.
Es uno de los tres conectores de adición formales de la lección.
exercises.solution:
**Furthermore,**

En un ensayo formal, para añadir un argumento al principio de una oración se usan *Furthermore*, *Moreover* o *In addition*, seguidos de coma. *Plus* es informal, *And also* es coloquial y *as well* va al final.

exercises.prompt:
Completa con un conector de consecuencia formal o neutro (una a tres palabras):

*The factory closed last year. ___, two hundred people lost their jobs.*
answers: As a result
Consequently
Therefore
Because of this
Because of that
As a consequence
So

feedback.message: Casi: *because* introduce una causa, y aquí lo que sigue es la consecuencia.

hints: La segunda oración es la consecuencia de la primera.
*As a result*, *Consequently*, *Therefore*…
exercises.solution:
**As a result** (o *Consequently*, *Therefore*): *The factory closed last year. As a result, two hundred people lost their jobs.*

Los conectores de consecuencia de oración van al principio, seguidos de coma. *As a result* es el más neutro; *Consequently* y *Therefore*, más formales.
